items.content_excerpt: $ONDS **( if you really dig, 3 systems are very different, and what they do, I won't do all your work)** AI Overview As of October 2026, Ondas Regna AI, Palantir Maven, and Anduril Lattice represent three foundational, yet highly distinct, pillars of the modern software-defined and AI-driven defense landscape. While they frequently collaborate—most notably through the Anduril-Palantir Consortium and Ondas' partnerships with Palantir—they occupy fundamentally different layers of the defense stack. Rather than competing directly, these platforms increasingly operate as a symbiotic hierarchy. In their ongoing joint deployment frameworks, Anduril Lattice acts as the frontline nervous system connecting the hardware; Palantir Maven serves as the overarching theater-level commander that handles the grand enterprise data; Regna AI functions as the localized, air-gapped safe box that allows tactical edge units to deploy specialized, secure AI brainpower without relying on external cloud connections

items.content_excerpt: $BTC.X $TAO.X $ASML $NVDA Iran War: Does It Really Matter to the Markets? Let's be honest. If oil keeps flowing through alternative routes and defense companies benefit from rising demand for weapons and ammunition, how much does this war really change the economic picture? Trump recently claimed that more oil is flowing through the Strait of Hormuz than before the conflict began. Meanwhile, markets continue to react to fears of supply disruptions and further escalation. Of course, the risks are real. But are investors reacting to actual shortages or simply to alarming headlines? Defense companies may benefit while other sectors face higher costs. That creates both risks and opportunities. My focus is shifting from the headlines to the bigger picture. If oil keeps flowing and parts of the industry continue to profit, perhaps the market impact is less straightforward than the news suggests.

items.title: Chip stocks plunged on Thursday as investors reacted to three major concerns: Tesla’s lower spending forecast, Lam Research’s weaker-than-ex
items.content_excerpt: Chip stocks plunged on Thursday as investors reacted to three major concerns: Tesla’s lower spending forecast, Lam Research’s weaker-than-expected outlook, and renewed worries about the AI boom’s dependence on external financing. These developments raised doubts about the sustainability of AI infrastructure investment and future demand for semiconductors and related equipment. Tesla’s decision to reduce its annual spending target was particularly concerning, as it suggested potentially more cautious investment plans among major technology companies. Meanwhile, Lam Research’s disappointing forecast pressured semiconductor equipment makers, while concerns over the financing required to sustain massive AI infrastructure projects added to selling pressure. The selloff hit the sector broadly: Intel fell 8.04%, AMD dropped 8.10%, Micron declined 6.26%, Nvidia lost 4.40%, and SanDisk plunged 8.51%. Optical-component makers also suffered sharp losses. $MU $INTC $AMD $NVDA

Just like SpaceX's paper write-up of its Boring Company stake, Tesla's balance sheet has also been utilized to anchor and fund the rest of the network. items.title: $AEP $AMZN $DOW $XE X-Energy recently announced a partnership with American Electric Power ($AEP) and Amazon ($AMZN) to bring a SMR project
items.content_excerpt: $AEP $AMZN $DOW $XE X-Energy recently announced a partnership with American Electric Power ($AEP) and Amazon ($AMZN) to bring a SMR project to Indiana. X-Energy and American Electric Power have signed a joint development agreement which covers feasibility work for a 960 MW SMR project in Sullivan County, Indiana. The plan calls for 12 Xe-100 units which will produce 80 MW of electricity each. The site sits near the retired Breed Generating Station which AEP owns. Amazon will provide project development funding as part of the agreement. This is the second deal under a larger plan between X-Energy and Amazon to add more than 5 gigawatts of nuclear power by 2039. AEP owns the land for the project and has decades of nuclear operating experience. Moreover, Amazon is paying for early development, while X-Energy brings the reactor technology itself to the table. https://www.barchart.com/story/news/8337772/x-energy-stock-surges-on-potential-nuclear-energy-deal

Management continues to expect adjusted EBITDA of approximately $1.6 billion, which equates to an annual adjusted EBITDA margin of approximately 33% to 34%. items.title: $MRNA Phase 3 melanoma data is finally out. Intismeran plus Keytruda cut the risk of recurrence or death 42% vs Keytruda alone, hazard ratio
items.content_excerpt: $MRNA Phase 3 melanoma data is finally out. Intismeran plus Keytruda cut the risk of recurrence or death 42% vs Keytruda alone, hazard ratio 0.58, p under 0.001, at 24.6 months of median follow-up. Two-year recurrence-free survival was 82.2% vs 70.0% for Keytruda alone. Distant metastasis or death fell 38%, hazard ratio 0.62, and after six months the recurrence hazard ratio was 0.42 in a pre-specified sensitivity analysis. Stock still closed down 17.6% at 202.63 dollars on 49.3 million shares. The earlier Phase 2 readout was a 49% risk reduction in a different population, and after a run of more than 500% this year, 42% was apparently not enough.

If patients and doctors could tell who got the vaccine, how independent was the call on when a recurrence happened? Trick or treat?

items.content_excerpt: $IREN NOV06 26C · still actionable Zone: $25.33 to $25.69 Invalidation: close under $24.86 Objectives: $26.74, then $27.84 The math: up 4.8% to the first objective and 9.1% to the second, against 2.5% risk on the invalidation, better than 3 to 1 to the second. Picture a beach ball held underwater. The longer it stays down, the harder it pops back up. That is this swing. IREN closed Thursday at 25.51 after printing a new low for the year, and the 14 day RSI sits at 25, which in plain words means the sellers have had the wheel for so long their arms are getting tired. Meanwhile the company says its 2026 capacity is largely sold out with about four billion dollars of contracted revenue, so the business is not broken even if the chart looks it. Earnings land November 5, inside this contract's window, which gives any bounce a date to run toward. P.S. Watch the 24.86 low first. As long as it holds, the washout has a floor. If it breaks, this idea is done.

items.content_excerpt: $CCI Bloomberg says SpaceX is in talks for access to at least 80,000 U.S. cell sites, and Crown Castle is one of the names approached. The stock jumped 9% after hours. Put the ask against the supply: CCI owns roughly 40,000 U.S. towers, American Tower about 42,000. SpaceX is asking for both networks combined, basically, and there were only about 158,500 purpose-built towers in the whole U.S. last year. Nothing signed yet. Bloomberg pegged the potential deals in the billions, and the carriers took the other side after hours, $T $VZ $TMUS down 4 to 5%.
